identity.name: Enzyme-treated starches
identity.chemical_class: Enzymatically modified starch (partially hydrolyzed carbohydrate polymer)

function.mechanism: Enzymatic hydrolysis of edible starch alters polymer chain length and rheology; in CFR enzymatic treatment can produce a nonsweet nutritive saccharide polymer (DE < 20).
common_food_categories: processed foods using starch-based texture control
beverage systems using modified starch functionality

adi.basis: No dedicated EFSA E1405 opinion/ADI identified in accessible sources. The 2017 EFSA modified-starches re-evaluation (12 starch additives) excluded E1405 and concluded no numerical ADI needed for that evaluated group.

efsa.key_finding: No dedicated EFSA E1405 re-evaluation located; nearest EFSA 2017 modified-starch opinion did not include E1405.

fda.notes: No direct E1405/enzyme-treated starch GRAS listing found in queried 21 CFR Part 184; regulated via Food starch-modified conditions in Part 172.

adi.basis: JECFA entry for ENZYME treated STARCHES shows ADI NOT SPECIFIED (2016, 1982); 2018 evaluation was specification-only.

concerns.summary: Recent cohort analyses reported associations between some food-additive mixtures (one including modified starches) and higher type 2 diabetes incidence; these are mixture-level observational findings and do not establish E1405-specific causality.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA: ADI NOT SPECIFIED for enzyme-treated starches (2016 and 1982 entries).
FDA: Food starch-modified may be safely used in food under 21 CFR 172.892 conditions.
No IARC monograph classification identified for enzyme-treated starch in checked IARC resources.

populations: high consumers of additive-rich processed foods
adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric ADI was identified for E1405 (JECFA uses ADI not specified), and no E1405-specific intake distribution enabling numeric exceedance calculation was found in retrieved sources.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evidence is broadly permissive (FDA conditional approval; JECFA ADI not specified) and no carcinogenic classification was found, but E1405-specific modern human outcome data are limited and most recent concerns are mixture-based rather than additive-specific.
key_factors: JECFA ADI NOT SPECIFIED history for enzyme-treated starches
FDA authorization under 21 CFR 172.892 with explicit process limitations
No dedicated EFSA E1405 re-evaluation identified in accessible sources
Recent epidemiologic concern is mixture-level and non-causal
